disease_context: TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancers, with loss-of-function mutations occurring in over 50% of all tumor types. It acts as a master transcriptional regulator of the cellular stress response, activating DNA repair, cell cycle arrest, and apoptosis — its inactivation permits uncontrolled tumor proliferation and genome instability.
difficulty_rationale: TP53 is a tumor suppressor requiring reactivation rather than inhibition; most cancer-associated mutations are missense changes that need allele-specific correction. The protein is largely intrinsically disordered outside its DNA-binding domain and lacks a well-defined small-molecule binding pocket in the wild-type form, making conventional drug discovery exceptionally difficult.

known_drugs.name: Eprenetapopt (APR-246)
known_drugs.mechanism: Restores wild-type conformation to mutant p53 by covalently modifying cysteines in the DNA-binding domain

known_drugs.name: Rezatapopt (PC14586)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective small-molecule corrector of p53 Y220C mutation that binds a druggable surface cavity and stabilizes the native fold

known_drugs.name: Nutlin-3a
known_drugs.mechanism: MDM2 antagonist that stabilizes p53 by blocking MDM2-mediated degradation; used as a chemical probe in research

disease_context: BRCA1 germline mutations confer a 50-85% lifetime risk of breast cancer and 15-40% risk of ovarian cancer; somatic BRCA1 inactivation also occurs in sporadic tumors. Loss of BRCA1-mediated homologous recombination creates a synthetic lethality dependency on alternative DNA repair pathways exploitable with PARP inhibitors.
difficulty_rationale: BRCA1 is a large (1863 aa) multi-domain scaffold protein functioning as a tumor suppressor; direct pharmacological reactivation of lost BRCA1 function is not feasible with small molecules. Therapeutic strategies instead exploit the resulting synthetic lethality (PARP inhibition), making classical structure-based drug design against BRCA1 itself extremely challenging.

known_drugs.name: Olaparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor that exploits BRCA1-deficient homologous recombination deficiency via synthetic lethality

known_drugs.name: Rucaparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2/3 inhibitor for BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer via synthetic lethality

known_drugs.name: Niraparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor with broader activity against HRD-positive tumors including BRCA1-mutated cancers

known_drugs.name: Talazoparib
known_drugs.mechanism: Potent PARP1/2 inhibitor with PARP-trapping activity for BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancer

disease_context: EGFR is overexpressed or mutated in many epithelial cancers including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), colorectal cancer, and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Activating mutations in exons 18-21 (especially exon 19 deletions and L858R) drive constitutive kinase activity and are the primary therapeutic targets in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.
difficulty_rationale: EGFR has a well-characterized ATP-binding pocket amenable to kinase inhibitor design, with multiple approved drugs; however, resistance through secondary mutations (T790M gatekeeper, C797S) and bypass pathway activation requires continuous innovation for successive-generation inhibitors.

known_drugs.name: Gefitinib
known_drugs.mechanism: First-generation reversible EGFR TKI targeting exon 19 deletions and L858R mutation in NSCLC

known_drugs.name: Erlotinib
known_drugs.mechanism: First-generation reversible EGFR TKI approved for NSCLC and pancreatic cancer

known_drugs.name: Afatinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Second-generation irreversible pan-ErbB inhibitor (EGFR, HER2, HER4) for EGFR-mutated NSCLC

known_drugs.name: Osimertinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Third-generation irreversible EGFR inhibitor selective for T790M-resistant and sensitizing mutations, sparing wild-type EGFR

disease_context: HER2 (ERBB2) is amplified or overexpressed in approximately 20% of breast cancers and in subsets of gastric, lung, and colorectal cancers. HER2-positive breast cancer was historically associated with poor prognosis, but HER2-targeted therapies including antibodies, TKIs, and antibody-drug conjugates have dramatically improved patient outcomes.
difficulty_rationale: HER2 has a validated and druggable kinase domain and extracellular domains; however, trastuzumab resistance emerges readily, complex HER2-HER3 heterodimer biology limits single-agent approaches, and the development of antibody-drug conjugates requires combining protein engineering with medicinal chemistry expertise.

known_drugs.name: Trastuzumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody targeting HER2 extracellular domain IV, inhibiting HER2 signaling and mediating ADCC

known_drugs.name: Lapatinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Dual reversible TKI of EGFR and HER2 intracellular kinase domains for HER2-positive breast cancer

known_drugs.name: Pertuzumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody targeting HER2 extracellular domain II, blocking HER2-HER3 dimerization

known_drugs.name: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
known_drugs.mechanism: HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate delivering microtubule inhibitor DM1 to HER2-positive cells

protein_name: GTPase KRas (Kirsten rat sarcoma viral proto-oncogene product)
disease_context: KRAS is the most commonly mutated oncogene in human cancer, with activating mutations present in ~90% of pancreatic adenocarcinomas, 30-40% of colorectal cancers, and 15-20% of lung adenocarcinomas. Mutant KRAS locks the protein in a constitutively GTP-bound active state, driving continuous RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling and uncontrolled cell proliferation.
difficulty_rationale: KRAS was historically labeled 'undruggable' due to its picomolar affinity for GTP, the absence of deep allosteric pockets beyond the switch regions, and a smooth guanine-nucleotide binding surface. Only recently have covalent inhibitors selectively targeting the G12C neoallele been approved; the other prevalent KRAS mutations (G12D, G12V, G13D) still lack effective direct small-molecule inhibitors.

known_drugs.name: Sotorasib (AMG-510)
known_drugs.mechanism: Covalent irreversible inhibitor selective for KRAS G12C, trapping KRAS in the GDP-bound inactive state via switch-II pocket

known_drugs.name: Adagrasib (MRTX849)
known_drugs.mechanism: Covalent irreversible KRAS G12C inhibitor with extended half-life, broad tissue distribution, and CNS penetration

known_drugs.name: Divarasib (GDC-6036)
known_drugs.mechanism: Next-generation covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor with improved potency and favorable combination profile

disease_context: BCL2 is the founding member of the anti-apoptotic BCL2 family; its overexpression, driven by the t(14;18) translocation in follicular lymphoma and by other mechanisms in CLL and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, enables tumor cells to evade programmed cell death and resist conventional chemotherapy.
difficulty_rationale: BCL2 has a well-defined hydrophobic BH3-binding groove that is targetable by small molecules; venetoclax validates this approach at clinical scale. Key challenges include selectivity among anti-apoptotic family members (BCL-XL, MCL-1) to avoid thrombocytopenia, and acquired resistance through MCL-1 upregulation or BCL2 BH3-groove mutations.

known_drugs.name: Venetoclax (ABT-199)
known_drugs.mechanism: Highly selective BH3 mimetic occupying the BCL2 hydrophobic BH3-binding groove, displacing pro-apoptotic proteins to trigger mitochondrial apoptosis

known_drugs.name: Navitoclax (ABT-263)
known_drugs.mechanism: Dual BCL2/BCL-XL BH3 mimetic with potent pro-apoptotic activity; dose-limiting thrombocytopenia from BCL-XL inhibition limits use as monotherapy

disease_context: CDK4 forms an active kinase complex with cyclin D1 to phosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein (RB1), releasing E2F transcription factors and driving cells from G1 into S phase. CDK4 amplification and cyclin D1 overexpression are frequent events in HR+/HER2- breast cancer, liposarcoma, and other solid tumors, validating CDK4/6 as proliferation targets.
difficulty_rationale: CDK4 has a canonical bilobal kinase fold with a well-characterized ATP-binding pocket; multiple selective CDK4/6 inhibitors are approved and widely used clinically, demonstrating clear target validity. The structural pharmacology is thoroughly understood, making structure-based optimization relatively straightforward.

known_drugs.name: Palbociclib (PD-0332991)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitor preventing RB1 phosphorylation and G1/S transition in HR+/HER2- breast cancer

known_drugs.name: Ribociclib (LEE011)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitor with demonstrated overall survival benefit in premenopausal HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer

known_drugs.name: Abemaciclib (LY2835219)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitor with continuous dosing schedule, single-agent activity, and approval in early-stage HR+ breast cancer

disease_context: VEGFR2 (KDR) is the primary signaling receptor for VEGF-A and the dominant mediator of tumor angiogenesis. Tumor cells exploit VEGF/VEGFR2 signaling to stimulate the formation of new blood vessels required for tumor growth beyond ~2 mm, making antiangiogenic VEGFR2 inhibition a cornerstone of treatment for many solid tumors including RCC, HCC, NSCLC, and colorectal cancer.
difficulty_rationale: VEGFR2 has a well-characterized RTK structure with multiple approved inhibitors; however, achieving selectivity among VEGFR, PDGFR, and Kit family kinases while avoiding dose-limiting vascular toxicities (hypertension, hand-foot syndrome), and managing rapid resistance through alternative proangiogenic pathway engagement significantly raises the therapeutic challenge.

known_drugs.name: Sorafenib
known_drugs.mechanism: Multi-kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR2/3, PDGFR-beta, and Raf kinases; first approved antiangiogenic for HCC and RCC

known_drugs.name: Sunitinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Multi-targeted RTK inhibitor of VEGFR1-3, PDGFR, KIT, and FLT3; approved for RCC, GIST, and pNET

known_drugs.name: Pazopanib
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective inhibitor of VEGFR1-3, PDGFR-alpha/beta, and KIT for advanced RCC and soft tissue sarcoma

known_drugs.name: Axitinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Potent and selective second-generation VEGFR1-3 inhibitor for advanced RCC

disease_context: PD-L1 is expressed on tumor cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells where it binds PD-1 on T cells to suppress anti-tumor immune responses. PD-L1 overexpression, often driven by IFN-gamma signaling in the tumor microenvironment or by oncogenic signaling (e.g., EGFR mutation), is a major mechanism by which tumors evade immune destruction across many cancer types.
difficulty_rationale: The PD-L1/PD-1 interaction interface is well-characterized structurally, multiple anti-PD-L1 antibody blockade agents are approved with clear clinical validation, and the biology is well-understood. Small-molecule disruption of PD-L1 dimerization and PD-1 binding represents an emerging approach with robust structural data and growing literature support.

known_drugs.name: Atezolizumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody that blocks PD-L1 interaction with both PD-1 and B7.1 to restore T-cell anti-tumor immunity

known_drugs.name: Durvalumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody approved for unresectable NSCLC following chemoradiation and extensive-stage small cell lung cancer

known_drugs.name: Avelumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody with retained Fc effector function for Merkel cell carcinoma and urothelial carcinoma

disease_context: MDM2 is the principal negative regulator of p53; it promotes p53 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and directly inhibits p53 transcriptional activity. MDM2 gene amplification occurs in approximately 10% of all cancers (and up to 20% of liposarcomas) and is mutually exclusive with TP53 mutation, making MDM2 a prime therapeutic target in p53 wild-type tumors.
difficulty_rationale: MDM2 possesses a well-characterized deep hydrophobic cleft that accommodates the p53 transactivation domain alpha-helix (Phe19, Trp23, Leu26); this pocket is highly druggable and has yielded multiple potent clinical-stage inhibitors. Extensive structural and SAR data make rational design tractable; the main challenge is therapeutic index (MDM2 inhibition activates p53-mediated toxicity in normal tissues).

known_drugs.name: Idasanutlin (RG7388)
known_drugs.mechanism: Potent selective MDM2 antagonist displacing p53 from MDM2 to reactivate p53-mediated apoptosis in p53 wild-type AML

known_drugs.name: Milademetan (DS-3032b)
known_drugs.mechanism: Oral MDM2 inhibitor with anti-tumor activity in p53 wild-type hematologic malignancies and liposarcoma

known_drugs.name: Navtemadlin (AMG-232)
known_drugs.mechanism: Highly potent piperidine-derived MDM2 inhibitor with picomolar affinity, in clinical development for AML and other p53 wild-type cancers
